blueprint.title: Daily Rollup Service Correction Drift
blueprint.scenario: A small analytics team runs a C daemon called 'rollupd' that reads a binary transaction log and answers per-day net-total queries over a simple line protocol. The analyst noticed that daily figures stopped matching the source ledger after a series of end-of-period corrections were posted three weeks ago. The codebase is ~1200 lines across six files: a record parser, a windowed accumulator with a state machine, a protocol handler, an index builder, an admin CLI, and a replay tool. The binary data file and its companion index are live on disk.
blueprint.instruction_draft: The rollupd service on port 7741 is returning wrong net totals for some days. Fix it so every day's net total matches the authoritative figures in /app/data/ledger_truth.tsv.
requirements: The rollupd service must be running on port 7741 after the fix
A QUERY <YYYY-MM-DD> request must return the correct net total matching /app/data/ledger_truth.tsv for every date present in that file
The service must handle at least 30 distinct date queries correctly at verify time, including dates with correction-then-reset sequences and dates with negative net totals
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm installs gcc, make, socat

Six C source files totaling ~1200 lines: record.c/h (binary format parser), accum.c/h (windowed accumulator state machine), proto.c/h (line protocol: QUERY <date> → TOTAL <amount>\nOK or ERR), index.c/h (day-boundary offset index), replay.c (replays data file to rebuild index), rollupd.c (main server loop)

Binary data file /app/data/txlog.bin containing ~8000 records: TYPE(1 byte) + DATE(4 bytes, days since epoch) + AMOUNT(8 bytes, int64 cents). Record types: 0x01=CREDIT, 0x02=DEBIT, 0x03=CORRECTION (delta to apply before next record), 0x04=RESET (zero the day accumulator)

Bug 1 planted in accum.c: when pending_correction flag is set and a RESET record arrives, the code applies the stashed correction delta to the post-reset zero baseline instead of discarding it; this is a state machine transition error only visible when a CORRECTION record is immediately followed by a RESET record in the same day window — looks plausible when reading but only wrong at runtime on specific sequences

Bug 2 planted in proto.c: the response serialization function encode_amount() uses a custom sign-magnitude encoding (sign byte 0x00/0xFF + 3-byte big-endian magnitude) for the TOTAL response, but for negative values the magnitude is computed as abs(val) >> 8 instead of abs(val) & 0xFFFFFF, producing garbage; this path only executes when the day net total is negative

Interaction: Bug 1 inflates CORRECTION→RESET day totals upward, preventing them from going negative, which masks Bug 2; fixing Bug 1 alone causes those days to return correct values but newly-negative days now produce garbage from Bug 2

The index file /app/data/txlog.idx is pre-built with the buggy accumulator state baked in; if the solver deletes/rebuilds the index before fixing both bugs, replayed totals for indexed days are wrong in a different way

Authoritative truth file /app/data/ledger_truth.tsv: tab-separated DATE\tNET_CENTS with ~150 entries including at least 20 CORRECTION→RESET days, 15 days with negative net totals, and 10 days where both conditions apply
A test client script /app/tools/query_client.sh that sends a QUERY <date> to localhost:7741 and prints the response, for the solver's convenience
rollupd is started by /app/run.sh and listens on 0.0.0.0:7741; the solver must leave it running
blueprint.internal_hint: Genuine difficulty from two runtime-only bugs: Bug 1 (accum.c state machine) only fires on CORRECTION→RESET record sequences — you cannot see it by reading because the logic looks plausible, only running queries on affected dates reveals wrong values vs truth. Bug 2 (proto.c encode_amount) only fires when net total is negative — and Bug 1's inflation hides those dates. The ordered danger: rebuilding the index with buggy code before both fixes are applied silently bakes wrong day-boundary offsets, causing replayed totals to be off even after patching. Correct procedure: (1) identify discrepant dates by querying vs truth, (2) instrument/add logging to trace which record sequences cause drift, (3) fix Bug 1 in accum.c (discard pending_correction on RESET instead of applying it), (4) observe that some days are now negative and Proto responses are garbled, (5) fix Bug 2 in proto.c (magnitude = abs(val) & 0xFFFFFF not >> 8), (6) rebuild the index only after both fixes are in place, (7) restart daemon.
blueprint.trap: A solver who fixes only Bug 1 will pass all the CORRECTION→RESET dates but fail dates with negative net totals (which are now reachable). A solver who fixes only Bug 2 will fail CORRECTION→RESET dates because Bug 1 still inflates those values above zero, making Bug 2's path unreachable and the fix look unnecessary. A solver who rebuilds the index before fixing both bugs will corrupt day-boundary offsets and see a third class of wrong answers that obscures the root cause.
tests: Test 1: Query 10 dates that have only normal CREDIT/DEBIT records — must return correct net totals (baseline sanity)
Test 2: Query 20 dates that have CORRECTION→RESET sequences — must return correct net totals (Bug 1 must be fixed)
Test 3: Query 15 dates that have negative net totals (no correction sequences) — must return correct encoded negative values (Bug 2 must be fixed)
Test 4: Query 10 dates where both CORRECTION→RESET and a negative net total occur on the same day — requires both bugs fixed in correct order

Test 5: Verify rollupd is still running on port 7741 and responds to a fresh QUERY for a date not in the solver's visible test set (generated at verify time from the same txlog.bin with a fresh correct implementation)

verifier_knob.name: number of request scenarios
verifier_knob.effect: Reducing to 20 queries (fewer negative-net and dual-condition days) makes it easier to pass with only Bug 1 fixed; raising to 80 queries adds more edge cases including multi-correction chains

expected_failure_modes: Agent reads accum.c, thinks the pending_correction logic is correct (it looks intentional), skips to proto.c and only fixes Bug 2 — fails all CORRECTION→RESET dates

Agent fixes Bug 1, sees some dates now correct, spot-checks a few negative-net dates with the provided sample, misses that encode_amount is wrong for negative values because the sample only shows positive days

Agent rebuilds the index (a natural step after patching C code) before both fixes are in, silently baking wrong offsets, causing a third failure class that sends the agent on a wrong investigation path

Agent patches proto.c encode_amount to use abs(val) & 0xFFFFFF but forgets the sign byte convention (0x00 for positive, 0xFF for negative) and outputs 0x00 for negative amounts — passes sign-magnitude format check but wrong value

speedrun: cat /app/src/accum.c  # spot pending_correction applied after RESET — visible bug
cat /app/src/proto.c  # spot abs(val) >> 8 in encode_amount — visible arithmetic bug
grep -v '^DATE' /app/data/ledger_truth.tsv | awk -F'\t' '$2 < 0' | head -5  # confirm negative totals exist
bash /app/tools/query_client.sh 2024-03-07  # sanity check current wrong output
nano /app/src/accum.c  # fix: on RESET, set pending_correction=0 instead of applying delta
nano /app/src/proto.c  # fix: change abs(val) >> 8 to abs(val) & 0xFFFFFF
invalid_failure_risks: The index rebuild ordering trap is avoidable by any agent who fixes code before rebuilding artifacts — it's not a reliable difficulty lever for agents who work methodically
Bug 2 (abs(val) >> 8 vs & 0xFFFFFF) is immediately visible by code reading — no runtime investigation required, undermining the 'only visible at runtime' claim
Bug 1's state machine error in the CORRECTION→RESET transition is also readable in source — the blueprint incorrectly claims these are 'runtime-only' bugs
The masking interaction (Bug 1 inflates values so Bug 2 path unreachable) only matters if the agent does NOT read source carefully; a code-reading agent bypasses the interaction entirely
encode_amount sign byte convention (0x00/0xFF) is an extra detail that must be precisely specified in proto.h or comments, or it becomes ambiguous what 'correct' means
The 3-byte big-endian magnitude custom encoding is unusual enough that verifier correctness depends on verifier implementing the same spec — risk of spec mismatch
Flakiness risk: if rollupd doesn't cleanly restart after pkill (port still bound), test 5 could fail spuriously

The blueprint says 'index has buggy state baked in' but if the solver rebuilds with correct code, this is fine — the trap only catches agents who rebuild with still-buggy code, which is a procedural error not a technical one
review.reasons: Both planted bugs are directly readable in source code — Bug 2's arithmetic error (>> 8 vs & 0xFFFFFF) is immediately obvious, and Bug 1's state machine error is visible to any careful reader of accum.c — making the speedrun only ~13 commands and genuine_difficulty scores 2, below the required threshold of 4. The blueprint incorrectly characterizes these as 'runtime-only' bugs; the masking interaction only forces runtime investigation if the agent skips source reading, which a skilled agent won't do. The ordered-index trap is also easily avoided by any methodical engineer who fixes code before rebuilding artifacts.
fixes: Make Bug 1 invisible to source reading: instead of a clear state-machine flag error, plant it as an off-by-one in day-window boundary detection (e.g., >= vs > in timestamp comparison) that only manifests when a CORRECTION record lands exactly at midnight boundary — looks like defensive coding when reading

Make Bug 2 invisible to source reading: instead of an obvious arithmetic operator swap, plant it as a subtle endianness issue — e.g., the magnitude bytes are written in little-endian order but the protocol spec says big-endian, which only matters for values > 0xFFFF (two bytes) and only for negatives — not obvious without knowing the wire format spec

Add a third file (e.g., index.c) with a subtle off-by-one in the offset calculation that is only triggered by the buggy accumulator state, creating a genuine three-way dependency that cannot be resolved by source reading alone — forces runtime binary tracing

Remove the query_client.sh helper and the truth file from obvious locations, requiring the agent to also reconstruct the expected values — or make ledger_truth.tsv only partially overlap with the test set so spot-checking passes but systematic verification is needed

Ensure the custom wire encoding (sign-magnitude) is complex enough that even after finding encode_amount, the correct fix requires understanding the full protocol spec in proto.h — add a checksum byte or length prefix that interacts with the sign byte

verdicts.reason: Ice phenology classification from satellite imagery is entirely unrelated to fixing a C daemon's accumulator bug in a binary transaction log service.

Both tasks involve fixing a running aggregation service whose computed totals drift from authoritative reference values due to a bug in the accumulation/weighting logic, verified by comparing output against a ground-truth file.
That task is about HMAC computation over WAL records with a refund-resolver lookup, whereas this task is about fixing net-total accumulation drift in a binary transaction log daemon.
That task involves HMAC chain verification over audit logs with a line-oriented protocol, not fixing per-day net-total drift in a windowed accumulator.
That task is about NDJSON schema validation correctness and performance in a Node.js pipeline, not fixing a C daemon's binary log accumulation bug.
